title: Facial recognition technology - the privacy law challenges in India
p1:
Your face is becoming a digital identity — but who controls it?

Many people think facial recognition is just a faster way to unlock phones or identify criminals. The bigger question is what happens when your face becomes data stored, analyzed, and shared.
p2: A surprising fact: unlike a password, you cannot change your face if biometric data is misused. In India, this creates a unique privacy challenge because facial recognition systems collect highly sensitive personal information, while rules around their use are still evolving under the country's data protection framework.
p3:
The real issue is not whether facial recognition technology is good or bad. It is about transparency, consent, security, and accountability. Citizens should know when their face is being scanned, why it is collected, and who can access it.

Technology can improve safety and services, but privacy cannot become an afterthought.
conclusion: Do you think India should allow wider use of facial recognition technology only with stricter privacy safeguards, or should its use be limited?
